uptake_ratio: MOUSE KIDNEY: Oatp1a1, Oatp3a1 and Oatp4c1 all HIGHER IN MALES than females. Oatp1a1, 1a6, 3a1, 4c1 are the highly expressed renal Oatps. Liver: Oatp1a1 male-predominant; Oatp1a4 and 1a6 female-predominant; Oatp1b2 liver-exclusive
direction_reabsorption_or_secretion: renal Oatp1a1 is apical = REABSORPTION; Oatp4c1 is basolateral = uptake from blood (secretion limb)
sex_or_hormone_effect: male-predominant renal Oatp1a1 in MOUSE, same direction as rat - so the Oatp1a1 argument is not rat-unique
source_table: Abstract (PubMed). NOTE: the abstract of Cheng X, Maher J, Lu H, Klaassen CD 2006 (PMID 16807376) states that renal Oatp1a1 and Oatp3a1 are 'female-predominant', which contradicts this 2005 paper and contradicts its own conclusion that renal Oatp expression is androgen-stimulated - treat the 2006 abstract wording as probably erroneous

study: Cheng X, Maher J, Lu H, Klaassen CD
expression_system: gonadectomised mice, GHRH-receptor-deficient little (lit/lit) mice, hypophysectomised mice, with sex-hormone or GH replacement
measurement_type: mRNA regulation
uptake_ratio: Androgens INCREASED Oatp1a1 mRNA in both liver and kidney; male-pattern GH increased hepatic but NOT renal Oatp1a1; renal Oatp3a1 induced only by androgen. Conclusion: 'In kidney, gender-divergent Oatp expression is exclusively caused by stimulation by androgens'
sex_or_hormone_effect: ANDROGEN-REGULATED in MOUSE kidney, i.e. the same hormonal control as reported for rat Oatp1a1 (Kudo 2002; Lu 1996; Gotoh 2002)
source_table: Abstract (PubMed); see the contradiction note on PMID 15843488

study: Buist SCN, Klaassen CD
expression_system: adult male and female 129J and C57BL/6 mice and Sprague-Dawley rats; branched-DNA signal amplification
measurement_type: mRNA expression, sex predominance and postnatal ontogeny
uptake_ratio: MOUSE: Oat1 kidney male-predominant; Oat2 kidney NO sex predominance; Oat3 highest in kidney, with higher female-kidney Oat3 only in 129J mice; Oat3 liver male-predominant. The most notable RAT-vs-MOUSE differences were (i) lack of Oat2 female predominance in mouse kidney (rat renal Oat2 is strongly female-predominant) and (ii) a less dramatic Oat3 male predominance in mouse liver
direction_reabsorption_or_secretion: Oat1/Oat3 basolateral = secretion; rat Oat2 apical, human OAT2 basolateral
sex_or_hormone_effect: the one clear rat/mouse species difference (renal Oat2) involves a transporter that does NOT transport PFOA, so it cannot explain rat-vs-mouse PFOA kinetics
source_table: Abstract (PubMed)

study: Buist SCN, Cherrington NJ, Choudhuri S, Hartley DP, Klaassen CD
expression_system: Sprague-Dawley rat tissues, branched-DNA signal amplification, days 0-45 plus adults
measurement_type: mRNA expression, sex and age
uptake_ratio: Rat renal Oat1 male > female at days 40 and 45; renal Oat2 considerably higher in females; hepatic Oat3 male-predominant; renal Oat2 rose dramatically at day 35 in females only
direction_reabsorption_or_secretion: Oat1/Oat3 basolateral = secretion; rat Oat2 apical
sex_or_hormone_effect: male-predominant renal Oat1 would INCREASE secretion in males, i.e. the WRONG direction to explain the longer male PFOA half-life - which is why Oatp1a1 and not Oat1 is invoked
source_table: Abstract (PubMed)

study: Buist SCN, Cherrington NJ, Klaassen CD
expression_system: gonadectomised and hypophysectomised rats with GH given by twice-daily injection (male pattern) or continuous infusion (female pattern)
measurement_type: mRNA regulation
uptake_ratio: Androgens (not GH) cause the renal Oat1 sex difference; the female GH secretion pattern causes the renal Oat2 sex difference; both androgens and the female GH pattern cause the hepatic Oat3 sex difference
direction_reabsorption_or_secretion: Oat1/Oat3 basolateral = secretion; rat Oat2 apical
sex_or_hormone_effect: mechanistic hormone attribution for the rat renal Oat sex differences
source_table: Abstract (PubMed)
